context.scope: Six attack surfaces of AcmeCorp CoreDB server (commit a1b2c3d) exercised using install-pkg (non-ASAN) build with crash/trap detection.

themes.title: Vendored directory client library trusts malicious server responses without bounds checking
themes.what_we_found: All four bugs live in the AcmeCorp DirectoryServices v10 libdirclient statically linked into AcmeDIRauthserver.so. The library decodes server-supplied fields (referral hostnames, TLV string-lengths) and copies them into fixed-size buffers without checking length, or trusts wire-supplied lengths that wrap to zero before allocation.
themes.why_it_matters: An attacker who controls or intercepts directory server responses can overwrite the return address inside coredbsysc's authentication path or corrupt heap state, giving code execution as the instance owner.
themes.root_cause_hypothesis: Frozen vendored DirectoryServices v10 client assumes the directory server is trusted infrastructure. Statically linked and unsymbolized, drifted out of any upstream patch stream.
recommendations: Rebase onto a maintained directory client or current vendor drop.
Add length clamps on referral-chase and TLV-decode entry points.
Make DIRS/StartTLS with cert verification the shipped default.
Consider disabling directory referral following in the auth plugin.

themes.title: Pre-auth PROTO handshake parser overflows fixed stack buffers, attacker controls return address
themes.what_we_found: Two PDU object decoders (DBNAME in coredb_pdu_sndpkt, NETADDR in coredbParseNetaddr) call coredbReadChars() with the client's PDU LL as copy length into fixed stack locals, without clamping. Both reached from pre-auth HELLO state, no stack canary, non-PIE coredbsysc.
themes.why_it_matters: Anyone who can TCP-connect to the PROTO listener can overwrite RIP in coredbsysc with no credentials. Credible path to remote code execution as instance owner; also one-packet unauthenticated DoS.
themes.root_cause_hypothesis: coredbReadChars() takes N directly from wire PDU LL; bounds-checking burden on each caller, which HELLO-state decoders don't honor. No -fstack-protector, non-PIE binary.
recommendations: Add checked coredbReadChars variant that takes destination buffer size.
Audit all PDU objects decoded in pre-auth states.
Rebuild libcoredb.so.1 with -fstack-protector-strong; link coredbsysc as PIE.

themes.title: FMT IMPORT parser trusts file-supplied length fields when copying into fixed buffers
themes.what_we_found: Two distinct root-cause bugs (7 raw reports collapsed): coredbimportrc.C:1930 FMTCUDTL→udtval[256] heap overflow → write-what-where, and coredbimportra.C:1134 A-record length → arec_buff[] stack overflow → RIP control. Both in engn/fmt/ FMT IMPORT path.
themes.why_it_matters: Reachable remotely with ordinary SQL privileges via SYSPROC.ADMIN_CMD('IMPORT … OF FMT …'). 'Can run IMPORT' becomes 'can run arbitrary code as instance owner.'
themes.root_cause_hypothesis: FMT parser treats file as trusted CoreDB-to-CoreDB interchange. No shared bounded-copy helper or up-front record-length sanity layer in H/T/C/A/D dispatch.
recommendations: Add hardened 'read N bytes into buf of size M' helper, reject file on overrun.
Validate header-declared lengths against record length and struct sizes at dispatch layer.
Sweep engn/fmt/coredbimport*.C and engn/fmtload/coredbload*.C for same pattern.

themes.title: Audit-archive extraction trusts record-length fields in archived log files
themes.what_we_found: coredb_audit_readrecord and readbuf_statement_values let a hostile .aud file dictate copy sizes — one via oversized field length, one via 64-bit size wrap to tiny allocation. Same (short)sizeof() pattern across ~20 sibling fields.
themes.why_it_matters: Reached via setuid-root coredbaudit CLI or NOT-FENCED SYSPROC.AUDIT_DELIM_EXTRACT inside coredbsysc. Local-to-root or DB-privilege-to-engine-takeover.
themes.root_cause_hypothesis: Audit reader assumes it only consumes self-produced records. No chokepoint bounds field length against remaining record bytes.
recommendations: Introduce bounds-checked 'read length-prefixed field' helper in coredbauditwr.C.

themes.title: acmeflacc trusts request length fields blindly, overflowing stack buffers in a setgid helper
themes.what_we_found: setgid acmeflacc reads TLV data_length from SysV msgq request without checking against message size or destination buffer. acmeflacc_catalog_node: memcpy into stack local with attacker-controlled length → RIP overwrite. acmeflacc_update_dbm_cfg: same field as pointer offset → wild read.
themes.why_it_matters: Any local user can launch acmeflacc and feed crafted msgq input — no CoreDB credentials needed. Stack overflow → code execution as acmeadm1 group, which owns the instance sqllib tree.
themes.root_cause_hypothesis: Request handlers assume caller is trusted CoreDB process. No shared 'validate length' helper. The setgid bit creates a privilege boundary the code was never hardened for.
recommendations: Add bounds check at TLV decode: clamp data_length against request_length and destination size.
Sweep all acmeflacc_* handlers for identical pattern.
Audit all setuid/setgid helpers under sqllib/security/.

cross_cutting_patterns.pattern: Unchecked length fields from external sources into fixed-size buffers
cross_cutting_patterns.note: All 5 components with findings exhibit the same root antipattern. Systemic coding convention failure.

cross_cutting_patterns.pattern: Integer arithmetic on untrusted size fields before allocation
cross_cutting_patterns.note: Integer overflow/wrap creates undersized buffers that subsequent copies overflow.
